sources.citation: Boehm, Kelly Kilgo. 2002 [published 2022 as SIL Journal of Language Survey Report 2022-007]. A Preliminary Sociolinguistic Survey of the Chhattisgarhi-Speaking Peoples of India. SIL International.
sources.note: Might list the Dhanwar among Chhattisgarhi-speaking tribes (identity confirmation); it is a survey, not a phonology, so no stress statement expected. sil.org could not be reached by automated download / HTML stub.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. VI: Indo-Aryan family, Mediate group: Specimens of the Eastern Hindi language. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing.
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accently: the Chhattisgarhi section is present (68 hits for 'Chhattisgarhi', Bilaspur coverage) but there are zero hits for Dhanwar/Dhanuhar/Dhanuwar, so LSI does not recognise a Dhanwar variety. Any stress content there belongs to Chhattisgarhi (chha1249), not to this key.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 RA. iso-639-3_Retirements.tab (current download). Row: dha | Dhanwar (India) | N (non-existent) | 2011-05-18.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative record confirming retirement reason N = non-existent, no successor code.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitter Chuck Fennig, SIL/Ethnologue). 2010. Change Request Number 2010-010: retire [dha] Dhanwar (adopted 2011-05-18). 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; p.2: 'There is no evidence that the language exists.' Rationale: 1961 Census is the only speaker count; 1991 Census, Singh 1993:87, Vaisanav 2004:6, Joshua Project 2009 and Russell 1916:488 all have the Dhanwar speaking Chhattisgarhi, Hindi and/or Marathi.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Dallas: SIL. Entry 'Dhanwar [dha]'.
sources.note: The record that created the code; classification 'Indo-Aryan, Unclassified' with no descriptive source; useful only to close the paper trail. Internet Archive copy exists but web.archive.org is could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. (assisted by Rai Bahadur Hira Lal). 1916. The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, vol. II. London: Macmillan. Article 'Dhanwar', pp. 488-501 (based on a monograph by Jeorakhan Lal, Deputy Inspector of Schools, Bilaspur).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.488: 'Like the Kawars, the Dhanwars have no language of their own and speak a corrupt form of Chhattisgarhi Hindi.' p.501: 'As already stated, the tribe have no language of their own, but speak a corrupt form of Chhattisgarhi.' Ethnography only (origin, septs, marriage, religion, occupation).
Nothing. Status: retired/bookkeeping; 'Retired as non-existent (2011, CR 2010-010)'; alt names Danuwar, Dhanvar; no descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
Nothing. Distinguishes Dhanwar Rai/Danwar of Nepal (a real Indo-Aryan language) from 'Dhanwar language (India), a purported language of the Dhanwar people of India, which does not actually exist'.
